issue.title: [NbrMgr] Skips NEIGH_RESOLVE table if the entries were populated before nbrmgrd starts

failure.body:
Currently nbrmgr subscribes to NEIGH_RESOLVE_TABLE using ConsumerStateTable, which is a notification-based consumer. It only receives entries that are written after it subscribes. If nbrmgr restarts, any entries already sitting in NEIGH_RESOLVE_TABLE from before the restart will not be replayed — there's no reconciliation or startup dump logic for this table in nbrmgr.

A fix proposal is to scan the NEIGH_RESOLVE_TABLE on init and process any pending entries before subscribing to new notifications.

resolution.title: [nbrmgr]: Reconcile pending NEIGH_RESOLVE_TABLE entries on restart
resolution.description:
**What I did**

Added reconciliation logic to `nbrmgr` so that on restart, any pre-existing entries in `NEIGH_RESOLVE_TABLE` are picked up and processed.

**Why I did it**

`nbrmgr` subscribes to `NEIGH_RESOLVE_TABLE` using `ConsumerStateTable`, which only delivers entries written after subscription. If `nbrmgr` restarts, entries already in the table are not replayed, leaving unresolved neighbors until the next route or neighbor event re-triggers resolution.

**How I verified it**

Added 5 unit tests:
- `ReconcileEmptyTable`: Verifies clean construction when no pending entries exist
- `ReconcilePendingEntries`: Pre-populates IPv4 entries and verifies they are reconciled on construction
- `ReconcileIPv6Entries`: Same verification with IPv6 entries
- `ReconcileSetNeighborFailure` and `ReconcileInvalidKeyFormat` for negative tests
